search_log: Searched "Answered Prayers" "Danielle Steel" with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, narrator, first person, third person, epistolary, and alternating-narration terms.

Opened the Penguin Random House, Penguin Random House Canada, AbeBooks, BingeBooks, Google Books, Open Library, Kirkus, and Goodreads pages; publisher and review synopses verified the work but their summary grammar was not treated as person evidence.
Targeted searches for an explicit scholarly or reputable whole-book POV description found no usable source; results were dominated by Truman Capote's different book of the same title.

Google Books offered only snippets and Open Library was preview-only. A late Chapter 24 passage was therefore checked as lower-tier interior corroboration, and no contrary first-, second-, or alternating-person structure was found.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person: the authorized opening excerpt externally narrates Faith and Alex while reporting their thoughts, and a late Chapter 24 passage retains the same external she/he position for Faith, Brad, and Zoe. q00152 is directly contextualized as part of that base narration. The I, we, and you forms in q00155-q00157 are dialogue or boundary-clipped material and do not establish a participating narrator. No searched source indicated sustained first- or second-person sections. Confidence is medium because the strongest authorized evidence is limited to the opening and the late-book corroboration is lower-tier rather than an explicit whole-book structural account.
